Throughput/latency goals we care about for the POC run:
- Support ~250 concurrent inference requests (approx. 1200 reqs/min) at peak
- P95 generation latency <= 350ms for 512-token prompts
- Steady-state run: 30 minutes after warm-up

For test cases: please include a representative mix: 60% short prompt (<=128 tokens), 30% mid (128–512), 10% long (>512) — we will share sample prompts in a follow-up.

Also, we'll need details on the test harness (how to run, required client config, where to push logs).

Marissa —

I can own the infra side. A few engineering notes for the run:
- Use our RIF-Harness v1.4 (containerized) and the "mix-profile" that matches Sara's distribution.
- Start with a 10-minute warm-up at 25% target concurrency, then ramp 5 minutes to 100% over i-1 increments.
- For cache baseline, let's run both: one cold-start pass and one warm-start (populate KV cache for repeated prompts). That gives AppForge visibility into both tails.
- Telemetry: we'll stream token-level latency, p50/p95/p99, and GPU utilization to the Drive runbook endpoints (logs go to s3://redwood-poc-logs/appforge).

Ben — can you author the exact ramp pattern in the runbook.xlsx and include CLI commands for invoking the harness?

—Vivek

Adding the concrete ramp we discussed; pasted below and added to runbook.xlsx.

Ramp plan (for 250 concurrent target):
- 0–10m: warm-up at 62 concurrent (25%) steady throughput pattern
- 10–15m: linear ramp to 125 concurrent
- 15–20m: linear ramp to 187 concurrent
- 20–25m: linear ramp to 250 concurrent (hold for 30m steady-state)

CLI snippet for harness run:
rif-harness run --profile mix-profile --concurrency 250 --duration 00:45:00 --warmup 00:10:00 --samples s3://redwood-poc-logs/appforge/run-{{ts}}.json

I've included telemetry points (p50/p95/p99, GPU %, mem, request error rate) and a note to capture raw prompts for post-run quality checks (redact PII).

—Ben
